q1.q: Is macOS Updates free and open source?
q1.a: Yes. The public code is MIT licensed and runs locally. Machine-specific files are intentionally gitignored.

q2.q: Will it install apps I do not already have?
q2.a: No. The updater only updates software already installed on the Mac. Supported missing apps are reported, not installed.

q3.a: The project is scoped to arm64 Macs and Homebrew at /opt/homebrew. Intel Macs are intentionally unsupported.

q4.a: Yes. Run bash update_all.sh --dry-run -y or bash scripts/report_update_coverage.sh to inspect coverage first.

q5.a: dev_sync handles optional private overlay files such as APPLICATIONS.md, UPDATES.md, .env, preferences, and cloud sync configuration. Import expands directory manifests, skips Git-tracked and excluded files, refuses symlink escapes, and leaves a recovery path if a swap fails.

q6.q: Why does mas upgrade use sudo?
q6.a: The project follows the current macOS/App Store CLI requirement documented in the repo, including the CVE-related Sequoia behavior.

q7.a: The current registry covers 43 internet-downloaded apps plus macOS, App Store, Homebrew, and CLI/npm tooling.

q8.q: How do I add a new internet app?
q8.a: Use scripts/scaffold_internet_app.sh, register the method and dispatch order, add i18n strings, then run bash run_tests.sh.

q9.q: How do I know an update actually landed?
q9.a: A mutation is reported only after the live Mac confirms it. Postupdate splits inventory field edits from observed package and CLI changes. Unknown pending stays unknown, not zero. A vendor CLI counts as updated only when a working --version exists.

q10.q: How do I update all apps on a Mac at once?
q10.a: Run bash update_all.sh. It updates the App Store, native CLIs and npm, Homebrew, 43 internet-downloaded apps and macOS in one ordered run. Preview it first with bash update_all.sh --dry-run -y.

q11.q: Does macOS Updates close my open apps?
q11.a: No. Apps you have open are never closed. The toolkit only quits what it launched itself, and running apps are protected at the bundle swap.

q12.q: Is it safe to run with sudo?
q12.a: It is built for it. sudo is requested at most once per run, never without a terminal and never during --dry-run. Only the App Store and macOS steps need it, and the code is open to review.

q13.q: Does it work on Intel Macs?
q13.a: No. macOS Updates supports Apple Silicon (arm64) Macs running macOS 13 to 27, with Homebrew at /opt/homebrew. Intel Macs are intentionally unsupported.

q14.q: How is it different from Homebrew or the App Store alone?
q14.a: Homebrew and the App Store each cover one layer. macOS Updates runs both, plus native CLIs, npm globals, 43 internet-downloaded apps and macOS, in a fixed order. It checks each vendor's feed first and reports only what the Mac confirms.

rules.title: Four rules every run follows.
rules.lead: Updating by hand means System Settings, the App Store, brew, npm globals, vendor updaters and DMGs. These rules hold on every layer.

vendor.title: Vendor truth before action.
vendor.body: Each app's installed version is checked against its vendor's own feed first. Apps that are up to date are left alone.

open.title: Open apps are never closed.
open.body: The toolkit only quits what it launched itself. Running apps are also protected at the bundle swap.

installed.title: Only what is installed.
installed.body: Supported apps that are missing are reported, not installed. Apps you removed by hand are never reinstalled.

confirmed.title: Reported only when confirmed.
confirmed.body: A result counts only after the live Mac confirms it. Stale feeds and timeouts stay visible as warnings.

stations.title: Seven steps, one fixed order.
stations.lead: The run above, written out. Each step names what it runs and what it refuses to do.
stations.caption: The seven steps of update_all.sh in run order, with what each one runs and its guard.
stations.flags: Skip a step or preview the whole run:

prescan.what: Scans /Applications, Homebrew and App Store receipts into this Mac's APPLICATIONS.md.
prescan.guard: Local inventory only. Another user's list is never imported.

appstore.what: Track 1: sudo mas upgrade on measured IDs. Track 2: AppleScript for iPad apps such as UniFi.
appstore.guard: sudo at most once per run, never without a terminal.

cli.what: Native vendor CLIs first (claude, codex, opencode, agy), then Node, Bun and npm globals.
cli.guard: A vendor CLI counts as updated only when a working --version exists.

brew.what: Formulae and casks with --greedy, then cleanup and brew doctor.
brew.guard: Orphan casks are skipped and cask downgrades are blocked.

internet.what: {{apps}} apps through {{methods}} update methods, each checked against the vendor's own feed.
internet.guard: Verified downloads: Gatekeeper, bundle ID and Apple Team ID checks, then a staged swap with rollback.

post.what: Refreshes APPLICATIONS.md and appends UPDATES.md atomically.
post.guard: Observed package changes are recorded apart from inventory edits.

macos.what: softwareupdate -i <label> -R, one label at a time.
macos.guard: Runs last because it may restart. Skipped when an earlier step failed.

coverage.title: {{apps}} internet apps, {{methods}} update methods.
coverage.lead: Only apps already installed are updated. The registry below is grouped by how each one gets its update.

brew_cask.name: Homebrew cask
brew_cask.note: Upgraded through Homebrew, with downgrade protection.

silent_launch.name: Silent launch
silent_launch.note: Opens the app so its own updater runs. Checked against the vendor feed when one exists, otherwise reported as launched (unverified).

github_dmg.name: GitHub DMG
github_dmg.note: Release DMG from GitHub, verified, then a staged swap with rollback.

keystone.name: Google Keystone
keystone.note: Google's own update agent. Used for Google products only.

appstore_gui.name: App Store Track 2
appstore_gui.note: iPad apps updated by driving the App Store with AppleScript.

manual.name: Manual
manual.note: No automatic path. Reported so you can update them by hand.

sparkle_appcast.name: Sparkle appcast
sparkle_appcast.note: Version read from the app's Sparkle appcast feed.

docker_cli.name: Docker CLI
docker_cli.note: Handled through the Docker CLI path.

mau_fallback_self_update.name: Self-update with MAU fallback
mau_fallback_self_update.note: Teams updates itself, with a verified Microsoft AutoUpdate fallback when Microsoft offers one.

chromium_updater.name: Chromium updater
chromium_updater.note: Handled through the Chromium updater path.

appstore.name: App Store
appstore.note: Measured IDs through sudo mas, plus Track 2 for iPad apps.

brew.name: Homebrew
brew.note: Formulae and casks, cleanup and brew doctor.

cli.name: CLIs and npm
cli.note: claude, codex, opencode and agy, then Node, Bun and npm globals.

macos.name: macOS
macos.note: System updates by label, always last.
